quotes.text: CliniCARE-Bench is constructed on top of three datasets from the MIMIC-IV database: the core MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2, and MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2
every tool invocation is logged and replayable

rationale: The paper names source datasets, versions, and platform/source database. It also describes patient-scoped retrieval and replayable logs as a route from task execution to source records.

quotes.text: credentialed PhysioNet users who completed the required training and executed the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement
retrospective, de-identified records from the inpatient, intensive-care, and emergency departments of a single major academic medical center

rationale: Origin and collection setting are documented as retrospective de-identified records from a single academic medical center. Licence/terms and consent/governance are covered through PhysioNet credentialing, training, and DUA requirements.

quotes.text: We sample 30 patients per scenario using stratification across Yes , No , and Indeterminate candidate strata

rationale: The paper reports a stated sampling design and cautions that the distribution is not clinical prevalence. It does not compare key patient features against a named target population.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet reports process defects and clinical safety-relevant abstention, but not dedicated unsafe-output and bias tests.

quotes.text: The patient-linked artifacts, which are derived from MIMIC-IV, will be made available on PhysioNet under its credentialed access policy

rationale: Credentialed access is a developer-side gating control for patient-linked artifacts. The packet does not report a measured contamination check such as overlap, canary, or held-out leakage measurement.

quotes.text: MIMIC data is reached only through a credential-isolated tool server, so no system can bypass the governed tools to read raw records.

rationale: The paper states runtime isolation from raw records and names the mechanism as a credential-isolated tool server with governed tools. This supports agent isolation from unavailable ground-truth/source material at run time.

quotes.text: MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2, and MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2
The production judge is GPT-5.5

rationale: The data sources are version-pinned, and the judge model is named. The packet does not pin software, harness commits, or model snapshots sufficiently to show a fully frozen release environment.

quotes.text: two clinicians independently vetted every scenario

rationale: Manual clinician review and model-assisted labeling provide solvability and correctness evidence. No scripted oracle solution is reported as run through the grader.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The benchmark tasks are retrospective audit/retrieval/reporting tasks and the packet describes no task that changes environment state.

quotes.text: Verdicts are scored by exact four-class match, with no partial credit.

rationale: The exact four-class verdict and extensive grounding/process metrics provide a design argument against trivial success. No empirical random or trivial-agent rate is reported.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet reports sixteen evaluated systems but no do-nothing or random baseline.

quotes.text: they agree on 97.9% of 1,331 category decisions
citation support requires LLM judgment

rationale: The benchmark validates its own automatic and LLM-judged evaluator components on benchmark outputs. It reports agreement and stability figures for grounding, process, and policy scoring.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. Repeated-run analyses are reported, but no seed, temperature-zero, or equivalent harness non-determinism safeguard is stated.

quotes.text: only 11 reach p<0.05 under a two-sided exact McNemar test and none survives Holm correction

rationale: The paper reports statistical testing for model comparisons on the development subset. It also cautions about paired case-level tests for close leaderboard differences.

quotes.text: In our primary protocol each case is run once
three independent attempts on all 148 cases

rationale: The headline full-cohort protocol states one run per case, and the repeated-run subset states independent attempts. No seed or sampling/decoding policy is reported.

quotes.text: Accuracy differs by at most 4.1 points (exact McNemar p\geq 0.46 )
A cell’s denominator is that system’s graded runs for that scenario, exactly 30 for every cell

rationale: The packet includes standard errors in several subset tables and names task/run/case denominators. It does not address clustering of tasks within patients, templates, or scenario groups as a variance issue.

quotes.text: Each system has three independent attempts on all 148 cases.
pass\mbox{\textasciicircum}k whether they always do

rationale: The benchmark reports pass^3-type all-runs reliability with run count. It does not report action-sequence agreement or final environment-state agreement across reruns.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. Model family names are listed, but not provider snapshot IDs or release dates; decoding parameters and harness commits/tags for reported results are absent.

quotes.text: SQL Fallback: A capped, read-only SQL interface
Policy-Document Tools: A lightweight file-access interface for listing, searching, and reading documents

rationale: The benchmark defines tool interfaces, so NA does not apply. The paper documents read-only/read-style side effects for some tool classes, but no machine-readable schemas or error/failure return semantics are in the packet; no S5 chunks are provided.

quotes.text: Parameterized, clinician-verified tools which support common record-retrieval operations across the MIMIC database

rationale: The paper says the clinical tools are clinician-verified, which is partial evidence of tool conformance. It does not disclose simulated/stubbed/no-op behavior or show such disclosure reaching the agent-visible surface.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet describes retrieval, computation, SQL, shell, and policy-document tools, but no action changes environment state or represents clinical orders, prescriptions, notes, or messages.

quotes.text: Each run produces a final report, a logged sequence of tool calls, the retrieved patient and policy evidence
we use the agent’s final report together with its logged tool-call trajectory

rationale: The paper names grader inputs, including final reports, logged tool calls, retrieved evidence, and LLM judgement. It justifies observable trace grading because private reasoning is not inspected, but it does not validate on injected known state changes with per-class error rates.

quotes.text: run with web search and fetch disabled
no system can bypass the governed tools to read raw records

rationale: The paper reports controls on leakage through web access and raw-record bypass during runs. It does not report held-out/private labels across all public surfaces or canary/provenance markers.

quotes.text: Verdict accuracy (%) per scenario, all 16 systems.
exactly 30 for every cell in the grid

rationale: The paper reports results by scenario, a named benchmark axis, with slice sizes. It does not report performance by patient demographic subgroup, even though the source EHR has demographic fields.

quotes.text: retrospective, de-identified records from the inpatient, intensive-care, and emergency departments of a single major academic medical center
made available on PhysioNet under its credentialed access policy and data use agreement

rationale: The paper states the patient records are real de-identified clinical records. It reports governance through credentialing and DUA, and gives data redistribution terms separately from the code release.
